findings.detail: In goal_loop_step (shiki_loop.py:2391-2399) a ready task with an expected_pr is snapshotted; if gh transiently fails, snapshot_pr returns {"number": pr, "error": True} (line 582). decide_task_action's ready branch (line 226) only clears when pr_state.get("merged") is truthy, so on an error it falls through to a plain dispatch WITHOUT clearing. Should gh recover by the next (review) cycle, the still-merged expected_pr can re-drive create_closeout_pr — the exact source-free-closeout bug this task fixes. The symmetric review path already waits on pr_state errors (lines 293-294) rather than proceeding. This is a narrow race (requires amendment-reopen + a gh error at exactly that snapshot + recovery) and is strictly better than the pre-fix behavior, so non-blocking; consider treating a ready-cycle snapshot error as wait_checks to close it.
findings.title: Transient snapshot_pr error on a re-opened ready task skips the pointer clear

scope:
In `scripts/shiki_loop.py`'s `decide_task_action`, stop reading a previous cycle's PR pointer as this cycle's completed work.

MEASURED 2026-08-06. Amendment PR #308 changed task `T-20260806T065143409817Z-dbdae1cf`'s design from staging the coordinator mirror to committing it — because staging had been proven not to clear a non-fast-forward merge. The loop was re-dispatched against the amended contract and its ENTIRE history was:
  cycle 1  dispatch             'task is ready for the implementer runtime'
  cycle 2  create_closeout_pr   'impl PR merged; push completion to main via a closeout PR'
`git log -- scripts/shiki_loop.py` showed one commit for that task, from BEFORE the amendment; the closeout (#309) changed only `.shiki` files. The amended contract was never implemented, and the CCA returned `complete`.

CAUSE: `:259-267` treats a merged `expected_pr` as proof the implementation is done — `if pr_state.get('merged'):` -> `mark_done` when `closeout_pr` is set, else `create_closeout_pr`. The task's `expected_pr` was 309, the CLOSEOUT PR, because the loop repoints `expected_pr` during a closeout. After the amendment re-opened the task, that pointer still described the previous cycle.

THE RULE: a task whose status is `planned` or `ready` and whose `expected_pr` names an ALREADY-MERGED PR is carrying a stale pointer — no work has been dispatched for the current cycle. Treat the pointer as absent and cut a fresh implementation. A task in `review` with a merged `expected_pr` is unchanged: that is the normal path into the closeout, and it must keep working exactly as today.

Detect it from the TASK RECORD ALONE — a non-terminal status plus a merged `expected_pr` cannot both describe the current cycle. Do NOT infer re-opening from an amendment marker, a ledger scan or PR timestamps.

FAILURE DIRECTION, and why this way round: clearing a pointer that was still live at worst re-opens a PR-less cycle and re-implements, which the loop already handles. Reading a stale pointer as done silently ships nothing — which is what happened, through a CCA that confirmed `complete`.

TESTS. `tests/test_reopened_task.py` (new): a `ready` task with a merged `expected_pr` decides to cut a fresh implementation, not `create_closeout_pr`; the same for `planned`; a `review` task with a merged `expected_pr` still decides `create_closeout_pr`; a `review` task with `closeout_pr` set and a merged `expected_pr` still decides `mark_done`; an UNMERGED `expected_pr` on a non-terminal task is untouched. `tests/test_loop_engine.py` and `tests/test_closeout.py` drive `decide_task_action` through this branch and pin the old behaviour — update them without weakening any closeout assertion, and add the measured sequence: an amended, re-opened task must not reach `create_closeout_pr` on its first cycle.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: a Spec Amendment merges, the loop is re-dispatched, and it produces no implementation at all — straight to a closeout whose diff contains no source change. The mirror then records a corrected contract that no code satisfies, and the CCA confirms `complete`.
  Measured 2026-08-06 on PR #308 / task T-20260806T065143409817Z-dbdae1cf, with the two-cycle history above.
  Root cause: `shiki_loop.py:259-267` reads a merged `expected_pr` as this cycle's completed implementation, and the loop repoints `expected_pr` at the closeout PR, so the pointer survives the re-open pointing at the previous cycle.
  Confirmed by the fix: clearing `expected_pr` by hand and re-dispatching produced a real implementation on the next run — 279 insertions / 102 deletions across three files, including the change the amendment required.
  Why it matters more than its size: an amendment is the only sanctioned way to correct a frozen contract. If its implementation can be silently skipped, the mechanism does not work.
  Reproducible when: a re-opened task with a merged `expected_pr` cuts a fresh implementation, and the ordinary `review` -> closeout path is unchanged.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Treat a merged expected_pr on a non-terminal task as a stale pointer
